steps.sop: The Software Engineer creates exactly one incident ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) for each triggered critical alert — no orphan alerts and no duplicate incidents. Done when the alert-to-incident mapping is 1:1 for the on-call window.
steps.verify: Reconcile alerts fired against incident tickets in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if every critical alert maps to exactly one incident with no orphans or duplicates.

steps.title: Assign severity and required fields per the incident matrix in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
steps.sop: The Software Engineer assigns severity per the approved incident-severity matrix v2 (Sev1 = business-critical feed down, e.g. a regulatory/finance or customer-facing feed fully blocked or >=1000 policy/claims records missing the 06:00 SLA; Sev2 = degraded with workaround) and populates affected DAG/business process, detection time, and on-call owner in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the workflow allows 'In Progress'.
steps.verify: Open the incident in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if severity, affected DAG/business process, detection time, and owner are populated and consistent with the matrix definitions.

steps.title: Diagnose using the failing DAG dashboards in Grafana
steps.sop: The Data Engineer diagnoses the failure using the DAG's dashboards in Grafana and cross-links the failing DAG run to the incident ticket. Done when the incident references the run and dashboard evidence.
steps.verify: Open the incident ticket; pass if it links the failing DAG run and the relevant Grafana dashboard used for diagnosis.

steps.title: Escalate per the escalation matrix in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
steps.sop: The Software Engineer escalates unacknowledged or unresolved incidents per the matrix — a Sev1 unacknowledged past 15 minutes auto-escalates to the secondary on-call and then the Engineering Manager — recording each escalation on the incident in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when escalations are timestamped on the timeline.
steps.verify: Open the incident timeline in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if each escalation step is recorded with UTC timestamp in matrix order.

steps.title: Disposition false positives and missing runbooks in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
steps.sop: The Site Reliability Engineer closes false-positive alerts with a 'false-positive' disposition (feeding alert tuning) and logs an 'SDLC-Exception' for any incident lacking a runbook, with the SRE lead as owner and a 10-business-day SLA, in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when every alert has a triage disposition.
steps.verify: Filter the window's alerts in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if 100% have a disposition and every missing-runbook case has an 'SDLC-Exception' ticket.

steps.title: Complete the incident timeline and record SRE sign-off in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
steps.sop: The Software Engineer completes the incident timeline (detection, ack, escalation, resolution/handoff with UTC timestamps) with the alert payload and paging log retained 24 months, and the Site Reliability Engineer signs off the triage record in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the timeline is complete and signed.
steps.verify: Open the incident in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if the full timeline, alert payload, and paging log are attached and a Site Reliability Engineer sign-off is recorded.

tasks.taskName: Triage demand to validate business need

steps.title: Pull the weekly intake queue in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
steps.sop: The Demand Manager pulls all incoming demand items (features, enhancements, defects, spikes) submitted for the current weekly intake window in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the queue is captured and no item sits in 'new' beyond the 5-business-day SLA.
steps.verify: Run the intake board query in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if all submitted items for the window are listed and none has been in 'new' longer than 5 business days.

steps.title: Validate required intake fields on each item in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
steps.sop: The Business Analyst validates that each item has requester, business sponsor, problem statement, expected value/ROI note, and strategic-objective link in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); items missing fields are returned as 'need-info'. Done when every item pending a decision has complete fields.
steps.verify: Inspect the queue in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if no decided item is missing any of the five required fields and incomplete items are in 'need-info'.

steps.title: Check duplication, alignment, and value assumptions
steps.sop: The Business Analyst checks each item for duplication against existing demand, confirms strategic alignment via the strategic-objective link, and flags items whose value hinges on an unvalidated assumption as 'need-info' rather than accepting them. Done when every item has an alignment and assumption check.
steps.verify: Open each item's triage notes; pass if duplication and alignment checks are recorded and assumption-dependent items are flagged 'need-info'.

steps.title: Apply the approved intake scoring model in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
steps.sop: The Demand Manager applies the approved intake scoring model (current version, weighted criteria for value, alignment, and effort) to each item and records the score and inputs on the ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when every item carries a score with the model version noted on the board.
steps.verify: Open scored tickets in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if each shows the weighted score with its inputs and the board records the scoring-model version.

steps.title: Route material demand to a business case and PMO review
steps.sop: The Demand Manager routes demand above the effort threshold (over 40 story points or cross-team) to a business case and PMO review before acceptance. Done when every material item links a business case and a PMO review record.
steps.verify: Filter items above the materiality threshold; pass if each links a business case and shows a PMO review before any accept decision.

steps.title: Record the triage decision on each ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
steps.sop: The Demand Manager records the decision (accept / reject / park / need-info) with rationale, triager, and timestamp on each ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) within 5 business days of submission; rejected/parked items carry a documented reason, and appeals escalate to the PMO Manager via an 'SDLC-Exception' owned by the Product Owner. Done when 100% of items are dispositioned.
steps.verify: Run the board reconciliation in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if items entering triage equal items with a recorded decision, 0 undispositioned at cutoff, and every rejection/park has a reason.

steps.title: Retain the board snapshot and record PMO Manager sign-off in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
steps.sop: The Demand Manager saves the intake board snapshot (retained 12 months for portfolio audit) and records the PMO Manager's approval of the cycle's triage outcomes in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the snapshot and sign-off exist.
steps.verify: Open the cycle record in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if the board snapshot is saved with the window id and PMO Manager approval is recorded.

steps.title: Extract quarterly scheduling telemetry from the Enterprise data warehouse/lakehouse
steps.sop: The Data Engineer extracts run durations, contention overlaps, and SLA-hit rates for all tier-1 and tier-2 pipelines sharing compute/warehouse capacity (typically 40-120 jobs) for the quarter from the Enterprise data warehouse/lakehouse. Done when the analysis dataset covers every in-scope schedule.
steps.verify: Open the analysis dataset; pass if it covers all tier-1/tier-2 pipeline schedules for the quarter with duration, contention, and SLA metrics per pipeline.

steps.title: Run the SCHED-OPT-1 contention analysis
steps.sop: The Software Engineer runs the approved scheduling-optimization methodology 'SCHED-OPT-1' (contention analysis plus critical-path scheduling) over the telemetry and proposes window changes; a change is proposed only if projected P95 runtime improves at least 5% or contention overlaps drop, without pushing any pipeline past its SLA. Done when the proposal list is produced.
steps.verify: Open the tuning proposal; pass if it references SCHED-OPT-1 and every proposed change shows a projected >=5% P95 improvement or contention drop with no SLA breach projected.

steps.title: Document each schedule change with rollback
steps.sop: The Software Engineer documents each tuned window: pipeline, prior schedule, new schedule, rationale, expected contention/throughput impact, and a rollback schedule. Done when every change record is complete.
steps.verify: Inspect the change records; pass if every tuned window lists all six fields and no change lacks a rationale or rollback schedule.

steps.title: Record tier-1 approvals on the change ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
steps.sop: The Software Engineer records pre-change sign-off for tier-1 (regulatory/financial-feed) pipeline changes on the change ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); tier-3 changes may be self-approved by the owning engineer. Done when every tier-1 change has an approval before application.
steps.verify: Open the change ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if every tier-1 window change shows a recorded approval dated before the change window.

steps.title: Apply the schedule changes in the change window
steps.sop: The Backend Developer applies the new schedules in a change window within 10 business days of the quarterly review, memorializing the effective date on the change ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the applied schedules match the documented changes.
steps.verify: Compare applied schedules to the change records; pass if they match and the change ticket shows an effective date within 10 business days of the review.

steps.title: Observe post-change performance for 2 weeks in the Enterprise data warehouse/lakehouse
steps.sop: The Data Engineer monitors post-change run durations and SLA-hit rates in the Enterprise data warehouse/lakehouse over a 2-week observation window: P95 runtime and SLA-hit rate must improve or hold, with 0 new SLA breaches, and pipelines still breaching SLA must be no more than the pre-tuning count. Done when the observation summary is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the before/after comparison; pass if P95 and SLA-hit rate improved or held, 0 pipelines newly breach SLA, and post-tuning breach count <= pre-tuning count.

steps.title: Roll back regressions and log SCHED-REGRESSION tickets in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
steps.sop: The Software Engineer rolls back any regressing window to its prior schedule within the same change window and logs a 'SCHED-REGRESSION' ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with disposition (re-tuned vs rolled-back) and a 5-business-day remediation SLA. Done when every regression is ticketed and reverted or re-tuned.
steps.verify: List 'SCHED-REGRESSION' tickets in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if every regressing pipeline has one with a disposition and the rollback or re-tune within 5 business days.

steps.title: Publish the tuning report and record Platform Engineering Lead sign-off
steps.sop: The Software Engineer publishes the quarterly scheduling-tuning report — schedule diff plus before/after metrics, tagged with the quarter and UTC timestamp, retained 24 months in the reporting repository — links it and the dashboard from the change ticket, and records the Platform Engineering Lead's approval at the quarterly sync. Done when the report and sign-off exist.
steps.verify: Open the tuning report under the quarter tag; pass if it contains the schedule diff and before/after metrics, links the change ticket, and shows Platform Engineering Lead approval.

steps.title: Identify SLA-breaching topics from telemetry in Grafana
steps.sop: The Data Engineer identifies the production streaming topics whose consumer lag or throughput breached SLA in the trailing 30 days using Grafana, capturing per-topic consumer lag, records/sec throughput, end-to-end p99 latency, and error rate. Done when every breaching topic has all four metrics captured.
steps.verify: Open the tuning-scope dashboard export from Grafana; pass if it lists each breaching topic with non-null consumer lag, throughput, p99 latency, and error rate for the 30-day window.

steps.title: Draft the tuning configuration with rollback reference
steps.sop: The Software Engineer drafts new partition counts, consumer parallelism, and back-pressure/rate-limit settings per topic with a rationale and the prior config version referenced for instant rollback. Done when the config diff covers every in-scope topic.
steps.verify: Open the config diff; pass if each in-scope topic shows prior and proposed values for partitions, parallelism, and back-pressure, plus a rollback config version reference.

steps.title: Replay peak load against the tuned settings in k6 / Gatling Streaming Load Testing
steps.sop: The Backend Developer replays representative peak load against the tuned settings in staging using k6 / Gatling Streaming Load Testing, verifying idempotent replay. Done when p99 latency and consumer lag are within SLA under peak with 0 dropped or duplicated records.
steps.verify: Open the load-test report from k6 / Gatling Streaming Load Testing; pass if p99 latency and lag are within SLA at peak load and the record counts show 0 drops/duplicates.

steps.title: Apply the tuned configuration under a change ticket
steps.sop: The Software Engineer applies the tested configuration to production under the change ticket, recording the pipeline config version/commit SHA. Done when the applied config matches the tested diff exactly.
steps.verify: Compare the applied production config to the tested diff; pass if they match and the change ticket records the config version/commit SHA.

steps.title: Attach before/after dashboard snapshots from Grafana
steps.sop: The Data Engineer attaches before and after dashboard snapshots from Grafana to the change ticket with timestamps. Done when both snapshots are attached.
steps.verify: Open the change ticket; pass if it carries a pre-change and a post-change Grafana snapshot, each timestamped, plus the config diff.

steps.title: Monitor the 7-day observation window in Grafana
steps.sop: The Data Engineer monitors the tuned topics in Grafana over the 7-day post-change observation period: 0 SLA-breach alerts, sustained consumer lag within SLA (e.g. p99 lag under 5s / under 10k messages), throughput headroom of at least 30%, partition utilization under 70% at peak, and no downstream error-rate increase versus baseline. Done when the observation summary meets all thresholds.
steps.verify: Open the observation summary from Grafana; pass if the 7-day window shows 0 SLA-breach alerts, lag within SLA, >=30% headroom, <70% partition utilization, and no error-rate increase.

steps.title: Close the change with Tech Lead sign-off or roll back
steps.sop: The Software Engineer closes the change with the Tech Lead's approval when the observation passes; on failure, revert to the previous config version via instant rollback, log the exception on the change ticket with owner = Data Engineer, and schedule a capacity/design review within 5 business days, escalating persistent SLA breach to the Platform Engineering Lead. Done when the change is closed signed or the rollback and exception are recorded.
steps.verify: Open the change ticket; pass if it is closed with Tech Lead sign-off after a clean 7-day window, or shows the rollback, an exception owned by the Data Engineer, and a scheduled follow-up review.

steps.title: Pull the closed findings list from the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC)
steps.sop: The Governance Analyst pulls all design-assurance and implementation-governance findings marked closed since the last pack update from the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC) for the in-scope services. Done when the closed-findings list with closure dates is captured for the period.
steps.verify: Run the closed-findings query in the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC); pass if the list covers all findings closed since the last update with their closure dates.

steps.title: Add a pack entry for each closed finding
steps.sop: The Software Engineer adds or updates an evidence-pack entry for each closed finding — finding ID, remediation description, closure evidence link, closure date, and approver — within 5 business days of the finding being marked closed. Done when every closed finding has a complete entry.
steps.verify: Inspect the pack entries; pass if each closed finding has all five fields populated and the entry timestamp is within 5 business days of closure.

steps.title: Link change tickets and fix PRs to each entry
steps.sop: The Software Engineer links each remediation entry to its change/remediation ticket and, where a code change was required, to the merged PR that delivered the fix. Done when every entry's links resolve.
steps.verify: Open each pack entry; pass if it links the originating change/remediation ticket and, for code fixes, the merged PR.

steps.title: Reconcile the pack against the GRC register in the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC)
steps.sop: The Governance Analyst reconciles pack contents against the finding register in the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC): findings closed in GRC equal findings closed in the pack (0 variance), every open-to-closed state change is mirrored with matching evidence and date, and open plus closed equals total findings for the period. Done when the reconciliation is clean.
steps.verify: Compare the pack to the GRC register; pass if closure counts match with 0 variance and every state change is mirrored with matching evidence and dates.

steps.title: Log EVIDENCE-GAP issues in the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC)
steps.sop: The Governance Analyst logs a GRC issue 'EVIDENCE-GAP' for any finding closed in GRC but lacking evidence in the pack, with disposition evidence-attached or re-opened and a 10-business-day SLA, escalating to the CISO if unresolved at period end. Done when every gap is ticketed.
steps.verify: List 'EVIDENCE-GAP' issues in the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC); pass if every evidence-less closure has one with a disposition and SLA date.

steps.title: Version the updated pack in the compliance evidence repository
steps.sop: The Software Engineer stores the updated pack in the compliance evidence repository with a SHA-256 hash, version number, editor identity, and UTC timestamp, retaining all prior versions. Done when the new version is stored with full metadata.
steps.verify: Open the compliance evidence repository; pass if the new pack version carries the SHA-256 hash, version number, editor, and UTC timestamp and prior versions remain intact.

steps.title: Record Enterprise Architect sign-off on the pack update
steps.sop: The Software Engineer records the Enterprise Architect's approval of the period's pack update; mismatches block period sign-off until resolved. Done when the sign-off is recorded against the cycle's pack version.
steps.verify: Open the pack version record; pass if Enterprise Architect approval is recorded for the period and no unresolved reconciliation mismatch exists.

steps.title: Assemble the change census in the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC)
steps.sop: The Tech Lead assembles the full census of merged PRs since the last architecture conformance review — identified by the Jira Fix Version and the Git tag range on the release branch, covering Guidewire PolicyCenter/ClaimCenter/BillingCenter integrations and surrounding microservices — and records it in the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC). Done when 100% of changed components are listed (no sampling).
steps.verify: Open the census record in the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC); pass if the component list matches the Fix Version and tag-range diff with no merged PR omitted.

steps.title: Map every changed component to an approved ADR
steps.sop: The Tech Lead maps each changed component to an approved ADR and the target-state reference architecture. Done when 0 components lack an ADR trace.
steps.verify: Inspect the mapping; pass if every changed component references an approved ADR ID and its target-state architecture element.

steps.title: Run the architecture fitness-function suite on the release branch
steps.sop: The Software Engineer runs the automated architecture-compliance/fitness-function suite on the release branch, verifying layering (no UI-to-DB direct calls), approved tech-stack usage (AKS, Azure API Management, Kafka/Service Bus), and that new capabilities are exposed via well-defined APIs; the run must show the same or fewer violations than the baseline main-branch run with no new blocker/critical issues. Done when the suite result is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the fitness-function run results; pass if violations are same-or-fewer than the main-branch baseline and 0 new blocker/critical architecture-rule violations were introduced.

steps.title: Reconcile changed components against the design package
steps.sop: The Integration Architect reconciles the count of changed services in the compliance run against the components listed in the design package (delta = 0) and diffs the dependency graph against the approved C4 container diagram. Done when both reconciliations are clean.
steps.verify: Open the reconciliation record; pass if the component-count delta is 0 and the dependency-graph diff matches the approved C4 container diagram.

steps.title: Log ARCH-EXCEPTION items for every deviation
steps.sop: The Tech Lead logs each deviation as an 'ARCH-EXCEPTION' issue with a disposition (waiver / remediate / reject), owner = Tech Lead, and a 10-business-day remediation SLA; open exceptions block the release gate. Done when every deviation is ticketed and dispositioned.
steps.verify: List 'ARCH-EXCEPTION' issues for the release; pass if every deviation from the suite or ADR mapping has one with disposition, owner, and SLA, and the gate is blocked while any is open.

steps.title: Record the conformance decision in the ADR log and ARB minutes
steps.sop: The Enterprise Architect records the conformance decision (conformant / conditional / non-conformant) with rationale, conditions, and their due dates in the ADR log and the ARB minutes. Done when the decision is documented.
steps.verify: Open the ADR log and ARB minutes; pass if the decision, rationale, and any conditions with due dates are recorded for this release.

steps.title: Export the conformance report to the compliance evidence repository
steps.sop: The Software Engineer exports the conformance report as PDF to the compliance evidence repository using the filename pattern 'archconformance-<release>-<yyyymmdd>.pdf', with Git commit SHA, ADR IDs, and reviewer signatures, retained 7 years and cross-linked from the change record. Done when the file and links exist.
steps.verify: Open the compliance evidence repository; pass if the PDF exists with the correct filename pattern, contains commit SHA/ADR IDs/signatures, and is linked from the change record.

steps.title: Record authorized Enterprise Architect sign-off and distribute the decision
steps.sop: The Enterprise Architect signs the conformance in the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC); the approver must differ from the change author, and if the EA is unavailable more than 2 business days, delegation follows the matrix (Solutions Architect first delegate, Tech Lead second) and is logged in the ARB minutes; the decision is distributed to the delivery squad, Tech Lead, Release Manager, and Product Owner. Done when sign-off and distribution are recorded.
steps.verify: Open the sign-off record in the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC); pass if the approver is authorized per the delegation matrix and differs from the author, and the ARB minutes capture the recipient list.

steps.title: Publish release contracts from the source code/CI-CD repository
steps.sop: The Software Engineer publishes every OpenAPI/AsyncAPI contract and consumer pact for the release from the source code/CI-CD repository to Pact Broker, with each contract schema version tagged and approved in the API catalog before publish. Done when the broker holds all contracts for the release candidate with approved version tags.
steps.verify: Open Pact Broker; pass if every contract/pact for the RC is present and keyed to a version tagged as approved in the API catalog.

steps.title: Validate each contract against its schema in the source code/CI-CD repository
steps.sop: The Backend Developer runs the CI contract-validation stage in the source code/CI-CD repository so every published contract validates against its schema (OpenAPI 3.x / AsyncAPI). Done when 100% of contracts are schema-valid.
steps.verify: Open the CI contract stage results in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if every contract validates against its schema with 0 failures.

steps.title: Verify consumer pacts against providers in Pact Broker
steps.sop: The Integration Engineer runs provider verification of the consumer pacts in Pact Broker for the release candidate's provider+consumer version pairs; provider verification also runs nightly against current consumer pacts. Done when verification results are recorded per version pair.
steps.verify: Open the verification matrix in Pact Broker; pass if each provider-consumer pair for the RC shows a green verification keyed to the correct versions.

steps.title: Reconcile broker contracts against the dependency map
steps.sop: The Integration Engineer reconciles the verified contracts in Pact Broker against the service dependency map so every declared integration has a contract, with 0 dependencies uncovered. Done when the reconciliation shows no gaps.
steps.verify: Compare the Pact Broker contract list to the dependency map; pass if every declared integration has a corresponding contract and the uncovered count is 0.

steps.title: Classify contract changes and process breaking changes
steps.sop: The Software Engineer classifies changes per the sensitivity rule — any change to the required field set or a type is breaking and triggers a version bump; optional-field additions are non-breaking — and logs each required breaking change as an 'SDLC-Exception' (owner = Integration Architect) with consumer notification, consumer sign-off, and a migration window. Done when no breaking change ships without a versioned contract and sign-off.
steps.verify: Review changed contracts; pass if every required-set/type change has a version bump, an 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Integration Architect, and recorded consumer sign-off.

steps.title: Re-run stale verifications in Pact Broker
steps.sop: The Integration Engineer re-runs any verification in Pact Broker whose timestamp is older than the release candidate, so every pair is 'verified' within the RC freeze-to-sign-off window; a contract must be verified for its provider+consumer version pair before deploy. Done when no stale verifications remain.
steps.verify: Check verification timestamps in Pact Broker; pass if every pair's verification is newer than the RC build and status is 'verified'.

steps.title: Confirm the release gate and record Integration Architect sign-off
steps.sop: The Software Engineer confirms 100% of contract pairs are green in Pact Broker at the release gate, archives the SHA-keyed CI logs in the source code/CI-CD repository (retained 400 days), and records the Integration Architect's approval. Done when the gate report is all green and signed.
steps.verify: Open the release gate record; pass if all pairs are green in Pact Broker, the CI logs are archived keyed to the commit SHA, and Integration Architect approval is recorded.

steps.title: Pull the Ready-for-Review story set from the requirements repository
steps.sop: The Business Analyst pulls all elaborated stories at status 'Ready for Review' for the current epic from the requirements repository (excluding 'Draft' and 'Backlog'), typically 15-40 stories per sprint within the active PI window. Done when the review set and its count are recorded.
steps.verify: Run the Ready-for-Review query in the requirements repository; pass if the result matches the epic's linked stories excluding Draft/Backlog and the count is recorded.

steps.title: Pre-check required fields on each story in the requirements repository
steps.sop: The Business Analyst pre-checks that each story has non-empty Gherkin Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, a testable definition of done, and a linked business owner in the requirements repository; required-field automation blocks the transition to 'Validated' if any field is empty. Done when every story passes the field check before the session.
steps.verify: Inspect each story in the requirements repository; pass if AC, DoD, and business-owner link are populated and no story bypassed the Validated-transition block.

steps.title: Flag material stories touching regulated flows in the requirements repository
steps.sop: The Business Analyst flags stories affecting regulated flows (rating, claims payout, PII handling) as 'material' in the requirements repository; material stories require compliance reviewer sign-off before build. Done when every regulated-flow story carries the flag.
steps.verify: Filter material-flagged stories in the requirements repository; pass if every story touching rating, claims payout, or PII is flagged and tracks a compliance sign-off requirement.

steps.title: Hold the stakeholder validation session
steps.sop: The Business Analyst holds the validation session with the business stakeholders and the Product Owner, following BABOK v3 elicitation methods per the BA Playbook v2.1, with the method version recorded on each story. Done when the session covers all Ready-for-Review stories.
steps.verify: Open the session record; pass if it covers the full story set and each story records the BABOK v3 / BA Playbook v2.1 method version.

steps.title: Disposition every story in the review log in the requirements repository
steps.sop: The Business Analyst records a disposition (Accepted / Changed / Rejected) for every reviewed story in the requirements repository review log, with 0 stories left un-dispositioned at session close; any acceptance-criteria change affecting more than 20% of a story's scope triggers mandatory re-validation with the business owner. Done when reviewed count equals dispositioned count.
steps.verify: Open the review log in the requirements repository; pass if stories reviewed equals stories dispositioned, and >20%-scope changes carry a re-validation flag.

steps.title: Raise Requirement-Clarification sub-tasks for disputes in the requirements repository
steps.sop: The Business Analyst raises a 'Requirement-Clarification' sub-task in the requirements repository for every disputed requirement, with disposition (accepted/rework/deferred), assignee, and a due date within 5 business days; failed stories move to 'Needs Rework' and breaches escalate to the Product Owner. Done when every dispute is ticketed.
steps.verify: List 'Requirement-Clarification' sub-tasks in the requirements repository; pass if every disputed requirement has one with disposition, assignee, and a due date within 5 business days.

steps.title: Publish the signed validation minutes
steps.sop: The Business Analyst publishes the signed validation minutes with per-story feedback under the epic space using the filename '<EPIC>-requirements-validation-vN', versioned and timestamped with attachments retained 3 years, and notifies the distribution list: product owner, assigned engineers, business owner, and scrum master. Done when the minutes and notifications exist.
steps.verify: Open the minutes page; pass if it follows the '<EPIC>-requirements-validation-vN' naming with version/timestamp and the notification to the four-role distribution list is recorded.

steps.title: Record Product Owner approval on the epic in the requirements repository
steps.sop: The Product Owner records the validation decision (approved/rework) on the epic's Validation field in the requirements repository with reviewer, date, and a link to the minutes; approval authority follows the governance RACI, with delegation to the Business Analyst allowed only for non-material stories and recorded in the delegation table. Done when the Validation field is set, targeting at least 95% first-pass approval.
steps.verify: Open the epic in the requirements repository; pass if the Validation field shows the decision with reviewer, date, and minutes link, delegation (if any) is limited to non-material stories, and the first-pass approval rate is measured against the 95% target.

steps.title: Enumerate changed code paths in the source code/CI-CD repository
steps.sop: The Software Engineer enumerates every changed public method and branch in the pull request diff in the source code/CI-CD repository as the test population. Done when the list of changed paths requiring tests is complete.
steps.verify: Review the PR diff in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if every changed public method and branch is identified in the test population with none omitted.

steps.title: Author unit tests for each changed path in the source code/CI-CD repository
steps.sop: The Backend Developer and UI Developer author unit tests for their changed paths in the source code/CI-CD repository: each test uses clear arrange/act/assert, a meaningful name, asserts behavior not implementation, and is deterministic (no reliance on wall-clock or network); no changed public method is left untested. Done when tests are committed with the code change.
steps.verify: Inspect the PR in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if every changed public method has a corresponding test following arrange/act/assert and no test depends on wall-clock or network.

steps.title: Run the unit test suite in GitHub Actions
steps.sop: The Software Engineer runs the suite on every commit locally and confirms it executes in GitHub Actions on the pull request. Done when the CI test job is green at the head commit.
steps.verify: Open the PR check in GitHub Actions; pass if the unit test job ran at the head commit SHA with all tests green.

steps.title: Evaluate the coverage gate in GitHub Actions
steps.sop: The Software Engineer evaluates the coverage gate in GitHub Actions: line coverage at least 80% overall, at least 90% on critical paths, and at least 80% on changed lines (enforced by the PR coverage diff), with the test count increasing alongside new public methods. Done when all three thresholds are met.
steps.verify: Open the coverage report in GitHub Actions; pass if overall >=80%, critical paths >=90%, and changed-line coverage >=80%.

steps.title: Run the mutation-testing sample on critical modules
steps.sop: The Backend Developer runs a mutation-testing sample on the critical modules touched by the PR to confirm assertion strength. Done when the mutation results are recorded for the sampled modules.
steps.verify: Open the mutation-testing output; pass if results exist for the sampled critical modules and confirm the tests kill the sampled mutants.

steps.title: Disposition failures, shortfalls, and flaky tests
steps.sop: The Software Engineer keeps the merge blocked on any red test; a coverage shortfall may be waived only via an 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Engineering Manager with a 10-business-day plan to raise coverage, and flaky tests are quarantined with a 'flaky' label and a 5-business-day fix SLA. Done when the PR is green or every gap is ticketed.
steps.verify: Check the PR state; pass if no PR merged with red tests or a coverage shortfall lacking an approved 'SDLC-Exception', and quarantined tests carry the 'flaky' label with SLA dates.

steps.title: Publish coverage artifacts and record Tech Lead sign-off in the source code/CI-CD repository
steps.sop: The Software Engineer publishes the JUnit and coverage reports as CI artifacts in GitHub Actions (retained 90 days, tagged with the commit SHA) and records the Tech Lead's review approval on the pull request in the source code/CI-CD repository. Done when the artifacts and approval exist.
steps.verify: Open the run artifacts in GitHub Actions and the PR in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if the JUnit/coverage reports are attached SHA-tagged and the PR shows a Tech Lead approving review.
